name: Outdoorsy
tagline: Peer-to-peer marketplace for renting RVs and campervans from private owners.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Outdoorsy is commission-based on bookings, not a subscription.

verdictSummary: Outdoorsy is a two-sided rental marketplace: the product is thousands of RV owners in places you want to leave from, plus the insurance and roadside assistance that makes handing a stranger a 30 foot motorhome survivable. You can clone the listing pages, the search filters, and the booking calendar in an afternoon. None of that gets a single camper van into your driveway. The hard parts are underwriting, claims, payouts, damage disputes, and the trust layer that convinces both sides to transact at all. This is not a tool you replace, it is a market you would have to recreate.
coreLoopDIY: A local listings-and-booking app where you track RVs you actually care about, their availability, and your own trip plans, with no payments and no strangers.
requirements: Your own list of rigs/owners to track, entered by hand
Optional: a map tile key if you want map view
whatYouLose: Actual inventory: the real value is other people's RVs listed near you
Insurance coverage and roadside assistance bundled into each booking
Escrowed payments, deposits, and dispute handling
Owner and renter reviews, which is the only reason either side trusts the other
Mobile app, trip handoff checklists, and support when the fridge dies in Utah
moatNotes: The insurance program is arguably as load-bearing as the listings. Personal auto policies do not cover renting your RV to strangers, and that gap is what Outdoorsy fills.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay Outdoorsy's service fee because it is the only practical way to get a specific RV, in a specific city, on a specific weekend, with insurance that actually pays out if something goes wrong. Owners pay because the alternative is Craigslist plus a prayer. Neither side is paying for software features, they are paying for the existence of a counterparty and a referee. A personal build can organize your own trip planning nicely, but it cannot manufacture either.
notes: The booking UI is a one-sitting build; the fleet and the insurance paper are not. The moat is marketplace liquidity welded to an underwriting program no hobbyist can replicate.
prompt:
Build a local-only "RV trip planner and rig tracker" web app. No marketplace, no payments, no strangers: this is a personal tool for tracking campervans and RVs I might rent or already own access to, plus the trips I want to take.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db
- Drizzle ORM for schema and migrations
- Tailwind CSS, no component library
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, single user, no auth

Data model:
- Rig: name, type (motorhome/travel-trailer/campervan/truck-camper), sleeps, length_ft, owner_name, owner_contact, city, state, nightly_rate_cents, mileage_fee_cents, source_url, notes
- Availability: rig_id, start_date, end_date, status (available/held/booked)
- Trip: title, start_date, end_date, destination, party_size, notes, rig_id (nullable)
- Checklist item: trip_id, label, done (boolean), category (pre-departure/onsite/return)

Features, in scope:
1. Rig list with filters: type, sleeps at least N, max nightly rate, state. Sort by rate or length.
2. Rig detail page showing availability as a simple month grid, plus an estimated total for a chosen date range (nights x nightly rate + mileage estimate).
3. Trip pages: create a trip, attach a rig, see a cost estimate, manage checklist items with a seeded default checklist (propane, water, dump station, tire pressure, insurance docs, campsite reservations).
4. A conflict check: warn if a trip's dates overlap an availability window not marked available.
5. CSV import and export for rigs so I can bulk-enter from my own research.
6. Seed script with 6 fake rigs and 2 sample trips so the app is not empty on first run.

Explicitly out of scope: payments, Stripe, insurance quoting, user accounts, email, push notifications, any external API, telemetry, analytics, scraping any rental site.

If you ever add a key, put it in .env.local and commit .env.example only. Nothing should be needed to run this.

Deliver: working app, README with setup in under 5 commands, and a one-paragraph note in the README stating plainly that this tool does not find RVs or provide insurance, it only organizes rigs I already know about.
